newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Clark sees Alliance support but no coalition.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Clark sees Alliance support but no coalition.

text.p: New Zealand Labour Party leader Helen Clark said on Tuesday she did not see the "slightest prospect" of a coalition with the left-wing Alliance but believed it would offer support on key policies to a Labour-led government after Saturday's general election.

"I don't think there's the slightest prospect of the Alliance entering a coalition, but the role they will play will be well understood by those who follow north European politics," Clark told Reuters Financial Television in an interview.
Under this system, Clark said, smaller parties gave informal support to minority governments by voting with the government on key policy measures.
Clark said Alliance economic policies "clearly can't be implemented", saying its proposed taxes would have a punitive effect on middle-income families.
Clark made clear she saw economic nationalist New Zealand First as Labour's potential coalition partner after the election.

New Zealand First has not ruled out a deal with the outgoing National Party government, but has said it would not do business with Prime Minister Jim Bolger, Finance Minister Bill Birch or Health Minister Jenny Shipley.
Clark said the departure of those three would prove too high a demand. "I think the National Party would look extremely silly if it were to agree to these conditions to stay in power," she said.
Opinion polls show Labour, New Zealand First and the Alliance look set to win a majority of parliamentary seats between them.
